scope: Six literature-led new Earth regions, three controls and twelve generated Idaho terrain windows; six existing planetary windows. Bounded purposive survey, not exhaustive/global discovery or a scientifically calibrated winner.
selectionRule: Published process/material/operations evidence chooses named candidates before terrain scoring. The added bounded grid generates unnamed terrain candidates independently; these do not inherit geological evidence from nearby named sites. A terrain score cannot validate a different evidence class.

regionalSearch.name: Southern Idaho terrain survey
regionalSearch.note: Analyst-chosen bounded region near the Idaho operations-study context. No claim that every sampled point is basalt or lies in a published BASALT footprint.

sampling.selection: Spatially distributed subset of a latitude/longitude grid; center-land screening only. Not exhaustive.

candidate.name: Lake Salda watershed
candidate.coordinateSource: https://assets.science.nasa.gov/content/dam/science/psd/astrobiology/for-researchers/early-career-field-research-fund/report_lc_garczynski_project.pdf
candidate.coordinateNote: Rounded location of Lake Salda reported by the field researcher; a regional window, not a specific sampling footprint.
candidate.condition: Fluvial/lacustrine sedimentation and Mg-carbonate investigation relevant to Jezero
candidate.literatureEvidence: Field observations and VNIR spectra of lake deposits provide a process/material analogue. This research does not reprocess the spectra or infer mineralogy from DEM values.
candidate.uses: Compare deposit types and plan observations/sampling questions for carbonate-bearing ancient lake environments.
candidate.limits: Modern water, living ecosystems and recent deposits differ from ancient Mars. This 32 km window includes a known lake and is not an approved wholly terrestrial ranking window.
candidate.withholdReason: Published lake footprint is inside this window. A current inland-water mask or approved land-only footprint was not acquired; no mixed land/water score is promoted.

source.title: Mapzen / Tilezen Terrarium mixed-source elevation tiles
source.datum: Source-dependent mixed DEM heights in metres; Web Mercator tile positioning (EPSG:3857). Consult original datasets for vertical datum and accuracy.
source.sampling: Direct RGB Terrarium decode without colour conversion; pixel-center-correct bilinear samples across tile seams into a 500 m grid.

landScreening.method: 5 × 5 samples against Natural Earth 1:110m land polygons; coarse coastline screen only, not a detailed inland-water classification.

coarse.method: 5 × 5 samples against Natural Earth 1:110m land polygons; coarse coastline screen only, not a detailed inland-water classification.

detailed.method: 65 × 65 point screen plus polygon-boundary intersections with the complete window; shared internal land-polygon edges ignored. Sample counts are not area fractions.

coverageAssessment.limitation: Natural Earth 1:10 million is generalized coastline mapping, not 10-metre resolution. Passing these checks does not verify all small water bodies, current shorelines, dry ground or field suitability.

source.caveat: Mixed elevation sources may include SRTM, USGS 3DEP/GMTED2010, Copernicus EU-DEM and NOAA bathymetry. Tile pixel spacing is not guaranteed source accuracy or effective resolution. Negative elevations are retained and are not used as an ocean classifier.

windows.researchReviewReason: Published lake footprint is inside this window. A current inland-water mask or approved land-only footprint was not acquired; no mixed land/water score is promoted.

candidate.condition: Impact-terrain reconnaissance, polar-desert field operations and instrument workflows
candidate.literatureEvidence: HMP has published field operations and instrument-testing history at an impact structure. Local terrain resemblance alone does not establish polar thermal equivalence.
candidate.uses: Evaluate observation planning and field/robotic investigation workflows in an established impact-terrain research setting.
candidate.limits: Terrestrial gravity, atmosphere, seasonal light and ground conditions differ from lunar permanent shadow. Specific deployment footprints and permits need separate review.

candidate.name: Yungay hyper-arid research region
candidate.coordinateSource: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9681764/
candidate.coordinateNote: Rounded field-study region coordinate reported in Methods, 24.05°S, 69.9°W. Precision is regional, not a surveyed plot boundary.
candidate.condition: Desiccation, halite microhabitats and observation/sampling in a hyper-arid setting
candidate.literatureEvidence: The published 2018–2019 transplant study measured environmental conditions and microbial responses. Published findings are context; raw logger and sequence data are not reanalysed here.
candidate.uses: Design questions about how sampling and environmental context affect interpretation in dry environments.
candidate.limits: Dry terrestrial soil and living halite communities do not replicate Mars atmosphere, radiation or an abiotic surface. DEM slope/relief does not measure aridity.

candidate.name: Río Tinto drilling-study region
candidate.coordinateSource: https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1089/ast.2019.2101
candidate.coordinateNote: Converted published deployment coordinate 37°43′30.99″N, 6°33′34.92″W; the DEM window is much larger than the drill site.

candidate.limits: River, mining and biological processes require separate footprint/water/geochemical review. A high terrain index cannot establish the published biochemical analogy or rover traction.

candidate.coordinateNote: Smithsonian GVP volcanic-field reference point; a reproducible regional window, not the exact BASALT EVA station or the whole monument.
candidate.condition: Basaltic field-science operations and communication-delayed observation planning

candidate.limits: Basalt origin and alteration state need their own maps/samples. Published NPS restrictions prohibit off-trail access in designated areas; no field deployment is approved by this study.

source.caveat: Native cells without altimeter returns are interpolated in the source; track gaps can reach 12 km. Posting is not effective measurement accuracy. This is not a rover-scale hazard map.
source.coordinateNote: Project study-window center uses the HiRISE DTM page approximate center -23.8 degrees, 326.3 degrees E, normalized to -33.7 degrees. HiRISE pixels are not ingested; this audit uses MOLA.
